correctness.rationale: Directly enumerate the two independent co-players, obtaining A=a+C0(q^2-omega*z^2) and B=A-k+2*C0*omega*z*y. At any interior equilibrium A=B=0, exact Jacobian differentiation gives tr J=2*C0*y[h*q*(x+z)+omega*z*(1-3*z)] and det J=4*C0^2*omega*x*y*z*(h*q*y-omega*z^2). The determinant-nonnegative case implies omega*z^2<=h*q*y and a strict trace lower bound, valid even at zero determinant; negative determinant gives a saddle. Other edges admit at most C, D, and one tangentially attracting DS root. For the admissible rational witness B0(z)=-2(z-1/5)(z-4/5), and C,D and z=4/5 have strictly negative required eigenvalues. The standalone exact-rational verifier checks independent payoff enumeration, Jacobian identities, and witness (1344 plus 101 cases); finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The model separates general contributions from quorum-triggered protective activity, so the smallest feasible group (N=3, M=2) is a natural structural boundary. The theorem answers a qualitative question left open by the N=5 numerical illustration: full three-strategy attraction is impossible at this size, yet maximum three-way bistable/tristable branching remains possible. The all-parameter trace-determinant obstruction and exact rational sharpness witness give both a structural restriction and a sharp attainable equilibrium count, relevant to how the minimal quorum changes collective-risk outcomes; not an arbitrary parameter lookup.
